1	# The hours step and the ladder
2	
3	**Every machine hour on the internal sheet says where it came from.** An
4	estimator handed "op 20: 9.5 min/pc" cannot tell a number read off a current
5	routing from one Fusion produced with library feeds, and those two numbers
6	deserve very different amounts of trust. So each operation carries its rung,
7	its path, its cutting-data basis, its setup and run separately, a range, and
8	the variance against every other source that exists.
9	
10	None of it reaches the customer. The customer quote carries prices; this file
11	is the internal sheet's business.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## What the hours step reads
16	
17	| Input | From | When it is absent |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| Routings | `routings` tab, consolidated dataset v4, or a routing file | No rung 1. Say so per part |
20	| Operation actuals | `operation_actuals` tab, dataset v4, or an actuals file | No rung 2. Say so per part |
21	| Geometry estimate | `../../../shared/contracts/geometry-estimate.md`, from `rfq-to-quote` step 7 or typed by the estimator | No rung 3. The internal sheet says the design step did not run and why |
22	| Machine classes | `Machine classes` table under `### Machining data` in the `## Plant context` block: Machine class, Work centers, Cell, Setup hours, Tool change min, Basis | Setup at rung 3 cannot be taken from the plant. Name it; the estimator supplies it or the op falls to rung 4 |
23	| Cutting data | `Cutting data` table in the same section (Material, Tool class, SFM, Chip load ipt, Basis), or a line `Fusion tool library: <name>` | The CAM path runs on library feeds and every op is `fusion_default`, rung 4. The feature path cannot compute a cut time |
24	| Variance flag threshold | `Variance flag threshold: <percent>` in the same section | Use 15%, and print it as **"15% — default threshold, not plant-set"** wherever a flag depends on it |
25	
26	A value tagged `Basis: assumed` in either table is used and labelled assumed on
27	every op it touches. It is the plant's number, recorded as a guess.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## The ladder, per operation
32	
33	Best available first. **The highest rung that exists for an operation is its
34	basis; every other rung that exists is shown beside it as a cross-check.**
35	
36	| Rung | What qualifies | What does not |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| **1 — Routing** | A routing for this part **and the revision being quoted**, cited by file and row or record. A routing that records no revision is usable, labelled *"routing revision not recorded — confirm it is current for Rev X"* | A routing for another revision. It is **superseded**: shown on the internal sheet as *"Rev 1 routing — superseded, not used"*, never priced from, at any rung |
39	| **2 — Closed-job actuals** | Actual setup and run hours from closed production work orders for this part and operation, `actuals_confidence: recorded`. Each work order named, the count from the figures block | Actuals flagged `probable_standard`. See below |
40	| **3 — Geometry-derived** | Hours derived from a geometry estimate whose `approval.status` is `confirmed` — or `draft` with the estimator's explicit say-so in this run, recorded — by the CAM path or the feature path, with `cutting_data_basis` of `plant_library` or `estimator_entered` | Anything on `fusion_default` cutting data. Anything from an unconfirmed model with no say-so |
41	| **4 — First principles** | Everything else: library feeds, a similar part's routing, the estimator's judgement, a feature path with no cutting data. **Always names what would firm it up** — *"a current routing, or plant SFM for 4140 with a 0.5 in carbide end mill"* | Never presented as anything firmer than it is |
42	
43	### `probable_standard` actuals never outrank rung 3
44	
45	Actuals the backflush check flagged may be the routing standard posted under a
46	work order number. They are shown, with their `confidence_reason`, and ranked
47	**below a geometry-derived estimate and above first principles.** Where the
48	standard they echo belongs to a superseded routing, they echo a superseded
49	standard: say that, too.
50	
51	### Actuals from an earlier revision
52	
53	Actuals carry the revision the job ran to where the source records it. Where a
54	drawing revision changed something this operation cuts or holds — the revision
55	history names it — those actuals are a cross-check for that operation, not its
56	basis. Operations the change did not touch keep them at rung 2, labelled with
57	the revision they ran at.
58	
59	### Units
60	
61	Setup in hours, run as minutes per piece. Where a source declares its unit,
62	converting minutes and hours is exact and is shown once (*"routing 7.00 min/pc
63	= 0.117 h/pc"*). **Where a source's unit is undeclared, that source is not used
64	for that operation** until the plant says what the unit is. The dataset's
65	`time_unit_flag` is carried onto the sheet.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## Setup and run, separately, at every rung
70	
71	Setup is a cost per job; run is a cost per piece. Each rung supplies both, or
72	says it cannot.
73	
74	**A source that gives only a lumped total has an unknown split.** State it, and
75	**never re-amortize it**: a total of 25 hours for 200 pieces is not 0.125 h/pc

78	show the lumped figure beside it at the quantity it came from.

1	# The cost buildup
2	
3	**"Cost basis shown" is the whole point of this skill.**
4	
5	An estimator will not trust — and cannot defend to a customer — a number with no
6	derivation. A quote that says *$14,720* is useless. One that says *$14,720, of
7	which $6,100 is material at the price we paid on PO-8841 in June, plus 8% scrap
8	allowance* is usable, defensible, and can be handed to a manager without
9	re-deriving it.
10	
11	So every line carries **its source and its assumption.**
12	
13	---
14	
15	## The seven lines
16	
17	### Material
18	
19	Quantity × price, **plus a scrap allowance** — you buy more than the finished
20	part needs, because some is cut away or ruined.
21	
22	Cite the price to one of three things, in order of preference:
23	
24	1. **An actual purchase price with its PO number and date.** The best basis
25	   available, and the only one that reflects what this plant actually pays.
26	2. **A current supplier quote**, with its validity period.
27	3. **Standard cost**, clearly labelled as standard, and labelled with its
28	   place in this list: **"standard cost (3rd preference, no actual-cost
29	   comparable)"**, with the reminder that standard cost does not say whether
30	   the last job of this kind made money.
31	
32	**No intake form is not a reason to build nothing.** "Price 250 of PN-4402-A"
33	in conversation is a minimal intake: part and quantity stated by the user,
34	everything else null and on the missing register. Build from the highest
35	preference available, which with standard cost only is the third, and label
36	it as such. A buildup with a labelled weaker basis is what the estimator
37	asked for; stopping on the missing form hands back nothing.
38	
39	**Always state the date of the price used.** Material markets move, and a
40	quote built on a price as of eight months ago is a different number from one
41	built last week. Where the price is volatile, say so and add a validity caveat
42	to the quote.
43	
44	### Labor
45	
46	For each operation: **setup hours plus run hours at this quantity**, × the
47	labor rate.
48	
49	The hours come from the ladder in `hours-ladder.md`, one rung per operation,
50	never a single rule for the whole job: a current-revision routing, cited; else
51	recorded closed-job actuals; else hours derived from the confirmed geometry
52	estimate; else first principles, naming what would firm them up. The rung, the
53	path and the cutting-data basis go on the internal sheet beside the line.
54	
55	A routing for a superseded revision is not an estimate of anything. It is
56	shown as superseded and never priced from.
57	
58	### Machine and burden
59	
60	Machine time × a rate covering the machine's cost of ownership. Same rule: the
61	rate cites its source, and the time cites its rung — the same setup and run
62	hours the labor line used, never a second estimate of them.
63	
64	### Setup
65	
66	**The one-time cost of preparing a machine for the job, amortized across the
67	quantity.**
68	
69	This is the single most important line for understanding a make-to-order quote,
70	because it is why unit price drops sharply with volume and why quantity breaks
71	exist at all. Show setup as a total *and* as its per-unit contribution at each
72	quantity — those two numbers together explain the entire shape of the price
73	curve to a customer who asks.
74	
75	**Setup and run are carried separately at every rung.** A source that only gives
76	a lumped total has an unknown split: say so, and never re-amortize it across a
77	different quantity — use the highest rung that carries a split for the break
78	arithmetic, and show the lumped figure beside it at the quantity it came from.
79	
80	### Outside processing
81	
82	Heat treat, plating, coating done by a vendor. Cite the vendor price and its
83	date, and note the lead time it adds — outside processing is frequently the
84	constraint on the promised date rather than the machining.
85	
86	**Where `supplier-quote-request` ran a sourcing event for this line and the
87	buyer recorded a decision**, the line is *sourced*: price it from the awarded
88	break in the selection record (`../../../shared/contracts/supplier-bid.md`)
89	and cite supplier, `bid_ref`, bid date, `decided_by` and `decided_at` on the
90	internal sheet. Its production lead time goes into the date check. A quantity
91	no awarded break covers is named, never interpolated; an MOQ above the quote
92	quantity or an expired validity is flagged on the line. A bid with no
93	selection record is cited as *a supplier quote, not awarded*. The supplier's
94	name and price stay off the customer quote.
95	
96	### Tooling
97	
98	Fixtures or dies. Often charged separately as NRE — non-recurring engineering —
99	rather than amortized.
100	
101	**Whether tooling is amortized or charged separately changes the comparison
102	entirely**, so state which, and state who owns the tooling at the end.
103	
104	### Margin
105	
106	Applied on top, per the configured rules, **and always shown as its own line.**
107	
108	**Never bury margin inside another line.** An estimator negotiating with a
109	customer needs to know exactly how much room they have, and a margin folded into
110	the material line is invisible to them and to their manager.
111	
112	---

1	# Commercial rates and credentials — where sensitive values live
2	
3	`onboarding` captures a small set of commercially sensitive values, and the
4	first rule of their handling is **storage**:
5	
6	> Storage — the encrypted/secret side of config, not a plain-text config file
7	> that could be committed to a repo or copied between customers. The rest of the
8	> config can live in the clear.
9	
10	This file is what that rule actually means in a running plugin, so no skill
11	has to invent it. Before this existed the phrase appeared across
12	`onboarding`, `quote-build` and `daily-production-report` with no mechanism
13	behind it — which meant a rate could never actually be stored, and
14	`quote-build` blocks the line a missing rate feeds. Every quote would have
15	blocked on labor and burden.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Two routes for a rate
20	
21	| Value | Variable | Plant profile field | Sensitive |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| Labor rate | `MFG_LABOR_RATE` | **Labor rate** | **Yes** |
24	| Burden / overhead rate | `MFG_BURDEN_RATE` | **Burden rate** | **Yes** |
25	| Margin rules | `MFG_MARGIN_RULES` | **Margin rules** | **Yes** |
26	| Downtime cost per hour | `MFG_DOWNTIME_COST_PER_HOUR` | **Downtime cost per hour** | **Yes** — derived from the three above, inherits their handling |
27	| Scrap costing basis | `MFG_SCRAP_COSTING_BASIS` | **Scrap costing basis** | No — internal-only, but not confidential in the same way |
28	
29	**Environment variables** — the same mechanism `.mcp.json` uses for a
30	connector's settings (`${FUSION_MCP_PORT}`), and a custom connector for its
31	credentials (`custom-connector`'s Limble example): the value is available to the
32	running session, and it is not a file in the repository. This is the stricter
33	route, and it wins whenever it is set.
34	
35	**The plant's rates file** — the `## Plant rates` block, written by
36	`onboarding` step 10 after the plant has seen the values and said yes, and
37	kept on the private `Plant rates: <company>` page in the user's Claude account
38	(`replies.md`, *The plant setup and the rates*). This is the route for anyone
39	who cannot set an environment variable, which includes every Cowork user. The
40	profile's `### Commercial rates` section then records each rate's state only.
41	Field layout is fixed by `../skills/onboarding/reference/config-profile.md`.
42	
43	Standard cost is **not** here. It comes from the ERP, where plenty of internal
44	people already see it.
45	
46	Everything else `onboarding` captures — export paths, shift boundaries,
47	vocabulary, the capability profile, templates, standards and clauses — is a
48	preference, not a secret, and lives in the readable config profile.
49	
50	## The four states
51	
52	Every rate is in exactly one of these. The `### Commercial rates` section
53	records which.
54	
55	| State | Block line | Prices the job? |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| **Set in environment** | `- **Labor rate:** set in environment (MFG_LABOR_RATE)` — the name only, never the value | Yes |
58	| **Confirmed in profile** | `- **Labor rate:** confirmed 71.00/hr - given by Pat Doyle, 2026-10-02` | Yes |
59	| **Placeholder** | `- **Labor rate:** placeholder 62.00/hr - assumed from the FY25 budget, not confirmed` | Yes, labelled **"placeholder rate — not confirmed"** |
60	| **Not set** | `- **Labor rate:** not set - see gaps` | **No** — the line it feeds is blocked |
61	
62	Margin rules hold the same JSON shape in both routes, because margin is rarely
63	one number:
64	
65	```
66	MFG_MARGIN_RULES='{"default":0.32,"by_customer":{"EXAMPLE-AEROSPACE":0.28},"by_job_type":{"prototype":0.45}}'
67	```
68	
69	```markdown
70	- **Margin rules:** confirmed `{"default":0.32,"by_customer":{"EXAMPLE-AEROSPACE":0.28},"by_job_type":{"prototype":0.45}}` - given by Pat Doyle, 2026-10-02
71	```
72	
73	## Resolving a rate
74	
75	**Every skill that needs a rate resolves it in this order, and no other.**
76	Link here rather than restating it.
77	
78	1. **The `MFG_*` variable**, if it is set in the environment. Check that it is
79	   set by name, without printing it. If the profile also holds a value for
80	   that rate, it is **not used and not printed anywhere**, the internal cost
81	   sheet included — not as a comparison, not as a conflict note. Say by name
82	   that it exists: *"labor rate from `MFG_LABOR_RATE`; the plant profile also
83	   holds one"*. Two numbers for one rate on the same sheet invite someone to
84	   pick the other.
85	2. **A confirmed rate in the plant's rates file**, the `## Plant rates` block
86	   at `rates_path` from `plant_setup.py find` (brought in from the private
87	   `Plant rates: <company>` page). For an older profile, the
